description:
FILED s488a (Opus, 2026-09-17) by task #1834's last question: four files have
been reported as SNAPSHOT movers by every companion run for months without
anyone being able to splice them, because their COUNTS are not stable.

THE FOUR (the s473t5d header's "rows-unstable" group): io/pvbm.t (23/5 run
alone -- three times, and on a 2ff53f8d extraction -- 20/8 inside a batch; NINE
recordings across s437, s438, s473t5d, s484d, s486c, s487, s488a),
io/crlf_through.t, io/through.t, uni/variables.t.

WHAT EXISTS AND WHAT DOES NOT, read in tools/run-perl-suite.pl:
  * `*rows-unstable*` (a file whose ONLY entry in perl-suite-fails.tsv is that
    marker) gates the ROW check -- `fails_rows_unstable` / `row_gated_here`,
    and --bless-fails never invents or overwrites it.  op/inc.t, op/hash.t,
    op/undef.t, op/utfhash.t and re/pat_advanced.t use it.
  * the #366 serial re-run LABELS a three-way disagreement
    ("THREE-WAY: snapshot %s %d/%d -- rows unstable? (serial recorded)") and
    then RECORDS THE SERIAL result -- it is a label, not an opt-out.
  * there is NO count-level equivalent: the SNAPSHOT block compares
    (status, C_ok, C_notok) against baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv verbatim, so a
    file whose count depends on load reports as a mover on every run.

THE ONE MECHANISM PROPOSED (not built -- it is a new column, so it needs a
ruling): a per-file BAND in perl-suite-run.tsv, written by hand like every
other row, in the shape the file already uses for `*rows-unstable*`:
    <rel> ... <status> <sig with `*count-unstable* <lo>/<hi>..<lo>/<hi>: cause`>
The comparison passes when the measurement equals ANY registered pair, and the
report prints which one it matched, so coverage is still visible.  Entry bar:
THREE serial runs of the file ALONE plus one on a `git archive` extraction of
the snapshot's own commit, all recorded in the row (io/pvbm.t already has that
evidence in its sig).  A file leaves the registry the moment one run reads
outside its band.

WHY NOT the alternatives:
  * blessing the batch number: a row that moves under load is then blessed as
    a behaviour, and the flap hides a real regression in the other direction.
  * the runner's serial re-run as the verdict: it already IS the verdict for
    two-way disagreements; the three-way case is exactly the one where neither
    number is the snapshot, which is what the band names.
  * one more marker file: the shortfall and the rows baseline are shared by two
    runners; a fourth registry for counts is the wrong direction (#993's whole
    point was ONE reading per question).

COST IF NOT DONE: every companion run's SNAPSHOT block carries 1-4 rows nobody
may splice, so "ZERO unexplained movers" can never be true and a REAL mover has
to be spotted beside them.  That is the same reading failure #1834 fixed for
the stable ones.

EVIDENCE ADDED s488a: uni/variables.t read TIMEOUT 1300/29413 in the parallel
pass and TIMEOUT 1300/24509 in the #366 SERIAL re-run of the SAME run (snapshot
1248/27934) -- one run, two numbers, because a TIMEOUT file produces whatever
the clock reached.  That is the strongest form of the case: no bless can be
right for it, and the runner already prints the THREE-WAY label saying so.
subject: the companion suite has no COUNT-level flaky registry: `*rows-unstable*` gates only the ROW check, so io/pvbm.t + 3 more report as SNAPSHOT movers on every run and cannot be spliced (a per-file BAND is the proposed one mechanism)
